title: The stories you carry
hookLine: a story for a kid who's stuck: Yunus in the dark, and the other stories the path has packed
tomorrow: which habits are still standing now that you're near the top?

cards: A kid who feels stuck, on homework, in a bad week, in his own head, rarely wants a lecture. He wants a story.
The Qur'an has one for exactly that: a prophet who walked away angry, ended up in the dark inside a fish, and said one sentence from there. Yunus.

He cried out in the darkness, in Pickthall's words: "There is no God save Thee. Be Thou glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer." And the next verse: "Then We heard his prayer and saved him from the anguish."

teach.b: That's the story for the stuck. But the path has packed a whole bag of them.

Adam, who slipped and was given words to turn back with; the Qur'an says, "Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him." Nuh, building on dry land while people mocked as they passed.
Ibrahim, watching a star, the moon and the sun set, and finding none of them was God. Musa, drawn to a fire in the desert. Yusuf, thrown down a well, who later forgave his brothers.
Yunus in the dark. And the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, once an orphan himself.
The Qur'an says why it keeps them: "In their history verily there is a lesson for men of understanding." They aren't decorations.
Yusuf. And the last stretch comes back with them: all settled, my last words, return, pleased, faces radiant, peace, peace, four words, a whole life.
You carried the stories for years. Now, on a hard day, they carry you.

how: Muslims tell the prophets' stories from the Qur'an to children and to one another, and some recite Yunus's words (21:87) in times of distress.

games.q: what does “the stories you carry” mean?
o: the prophets' stories, kept close for hard days
family stories passed down from your grandparents
the history of how the Qur'an was written down

games.q: which story, for which day — tap the pairs.
p: for when you're stuck in the dark
watched the star, moon and sun set

s: in the Qur'an, Yunus waited out the dark in silence
he cried out: there is no God save Thee. and he was heard.
the Qur'an says there is a lesson in the prophets' stories for people of understanding
12:111: in their history verily there is a lesson.
the Qur'an's story of Adam ends with Allah relenting toward him
2:37: he received words from his Lord, and He relented toward him.

games.q: a friend's younger sister got caught lying to her parents and says, 'i ruined everything; they'll never trust me again.' which story from the path fits best?
o: Adam: he slipped, was given words to turn back with, and was forgiven.
Yunus: walk away until things calm down, then come back.
Nuh: ignore whatever people are saying about you.
games.why: Adam's story is the one for a slip: words to turn back with, and a Lord who relents. Yunus is for the dark; Nuh for being mocked.

practice: Pick the one story from the path you'd most want to be able to tell a child. Run through it in your head in a few short sentences: who, what went wrong, what they said or did, what happened next.
If you like, write its key line by hand.

wordCard.voice: The stories you carry: the prophets' stories from the Qur'an, from Adam to Yunus to the Prophet Muhammad, kept close as a toolkit for hard days.

orig.note: Arabic: Yunus, the prophet known in the Bible as Jonah; also called Dhu'n-Nun, the one of the fish.

carryVoice: One line for a hard day: the stories carry you, the way a fish once carried Yunus to shore. See you at the next step of the summit.

sources.q: There is no God save Thee. Be Thou glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer.
Then We heard his prayer and saved him from the anguish.
Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him.
In their history verily there is a lesson for men of understanding.

sources.ref: Qur'an 11:38 (Nuh mocked as he builds), 6:76–79 (Ibrahim and the setting star, moon and sun), 20:10 (Musa sees a fire), 12:15 and 12:92 (Yusuf in the well; his forgiveness), 37:142 (the fish swallows Yunus), 93:6 (the Prophet an orphan)
